proxy_language: Proto-Berber (Proto-Amazigh / Proto-Libyco-Berber), with Proto-Afroasiatic roots as a deeper fallback
proxy_rationale: The Capsian (c. 10,000-6,000 BCE, Algeria/Tunisia, escargotieres) left no texts. The most defensible proxy is Proto-Berber, the ancestor of the Amazigh languages (Tamazight, Tashelhit, Kabyle, Tuareg, Zenaga, Siwi), spoken in exactly this region. Proto-Berber is only reconstructed to roughly the last 3-4 millennia, so its link to the Capsian is speculative; some scholars (e.g. Camps, Ehret) propose Capsian people as ancestors of Berber speakers, but this is contested. Afroasiatic roots (Semitic, Egyptian, Cushitic cognates) are a fallback for very basic vocabulary. Labels are reconstructive models, not claims of attestation.
phonology: Proto-Berber/Tamazight-type consonantism: stops *b *t *d *k *g *q (uvular), fricatives *f *s *z *sh *zh *x *gh (uvular) *h *H (pharyngeal) *3 (ayin), sonorants *m *n *l *r, glides *w *y. Emphatic (pharyngealized) consonants (t., d., s., z., r., l.) are marked with a dot or capital in transliteration. Labialized velars/uvulars (kw, gw, qw) and geminate consonants are contrastive; gemination is meaningful. Vowel system is minimal: *a, *i, *u, plus an epenthetic schwa (e) in modern forms (a reconstructed three-vowel system is generally assumed for proto-forms).
phonotactics: Syllable shapes CV, CVC, V, VC; no phonemic V-initial restriction in Tuareg (word-initial vowel is usual as the masculine noun prefix). Berber permits consonant clusters and even syllabic consonants in modern Tashelhit; for a game-safe proto-style, prefer CV(C) syllables with limited clusters and geminates. Words typically 2-3 syllables. Word-final: vowels or consonants, both allowed. No long vowels in the standard transliteration. Stress is largely predictable and not written.
orthography: Use Latin Berber scholarly transliteration: a, i, u, e (schwa), b d f g gh h k kh l m n q r s sh t w x y z zh, plus gemination as doubled letters (tt, ss, ll) and labialization as w after a velar (kw, gw). Avoid p, v, o, c, j.
morphology: Triconsonantal-ish roots (consonantal root with vocalic patterns) as in Afroasiatic. Nouns carry a gender-number frame: masculine singular a-/i-/u- ... ; feminine t-...-t (circumfixed); plural by suffix -en/-in (masc.) and -in/-at (fem.) or internal 'broken' plural. State opposition: free state vs annexed state (vowel prefix drops, e.g. a-ghrum vs w-ghrum). Verbal derivation by prefixes: s- (causative, e.g. s-ezzu 'make go'), m- (reciprocal), tt- (passive/habitual); agent nouns by am-/an-/ama- (e.g. am-...). Abstract/derivational noun prefixes: tam- / tim- (feminine collective or abstract), t- ... -t (diminutive/feminine).
compounding: Berber seldom forms true compounds; instead uses the annexed-state genitive construction 'head + n + modifier' (n = 'of'). Examples: 'house of X' = tigemmi n X; 'son of X' = u/ult/ayt, with 'ayt' (people of) used for group names ('Ayt X'). Agent/maker nouns use the prefix am-/ama-/an- + verbal noun or root ('one who does/has'). Place names often use 'ighzer n X' (river of X), 'adrar n X' (mountain of X), 'tamda n X' (lake of X). A linker n is the standard genitive particle; no case endings.
noun_phrase_order: Head noun first, then modifiers: noun + adjective (a-ghrum a-meqran 'big bread') and noun + n + genitive noun. Demonstratives and possessives are postposed (clitic -nnes etc.). Numerals precede the noun in many varieties. Names thus read 'Head-n-Modifier'.

attested_roots.gloss: mouflon/rock animal (Tuareg attested for wild sheep)
mare (fem. of horse; avoid as Capsian-era)
fire (Tuareg: tafuk is sun; fire varies as tmes)

notes: Link between Capsian culture and Berber languages is speculative; treat names as plausible North African flavor rather than reconstructed Capsian speech. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since Berber is not Goidelic. Existing game strings (khududngi, muchab, qizwo, lukhuba) contain dng, ch, and o clusters foreign to Berber, so rebuild on CV(C) patterns with the n-genitive. Sun/moon/animal glosses are modern Tuareg/Tashelhit/Kabyle forms, not reconstructed Capsian.
